paragraphs.text: [Ripe pu’er](shou:definition) from Yunnan, made in the 1990s and never pressed into a cake. It has stayed as open leaf through its years in storage in Guangzhou, with more air moving through it than a pressed tea would have. The [wet-pile method](shou:wet-piling) behind it only reached production in 1973, so this lot comes from the style’s early decades.
At thirty-one years it sits well inside what the trade counts as [aged ripe pu’er](shou:age-aged). Where and how it was kept has shaped the leaf as much as time has.

brewing.text: Loose leaf needs no breaking apart, so measure it straight into the pot. Use boiling water, about 7 grams to 100 ml, one quick rinse, then short steeps that lengthen as the leaf opens. Old ripe tea like this gives eight or more good cups.

notice.text: A smooth, deep cup with woody, date-like or medicinal notes, which the trade calls aged aroma.
